verbatim_transcript: Limitations of traditional n-gram LM are: 1) Traditional n-gram LMs mostly fail to capture long-range dependencies. 2) N-gram LMs generally face data sparsity as enough data for larger n-gram is rare or not available.

Transformers process all tokens in parallel using self-attention which does not have any inherent sequential order. Therefore positional encoding is added to token embeddings to inject word order information.

Encoder-only architectures (like BERT) take an input sequence and use bidirectional self-attention to generate representations for classification and understanding. Decoder architectures (like GPT) use causal masked attention to generate new tokens autoregressively.

Masked Attention: General self-attention allows tokens to attend to all positions. To forbid models from seeing future tokens in advance (which is cheating) in autoregressive language models, we mask positions greater than current position by setting attention input to -infinity so softmax comes to 0. Used in GPT for causal next-token generation.
Given Q = [1, 0], K1 = [1, 1], K2 = [0, 1]. Dot products: Score for K1 = Q . K1 = 1*1 + 0*1 = 1. Score for K2 = Q . K2 = 1*0 + 0*1 = 0.

Softmax([1, 0]): for k1, a1 = e^1 / (e^1 + e^0) = e / (e+1) approx 0.73 (student rounded to 0.7). for k2, a2 = e^0 / (e^1 + e^0) = 1 / (e+1) approx 0.27 (student rounded to 0.3). Attention weights A = [0.7, 0.3].

Layer normalization is applied in each transformer block because layer normalization is generally used for normalizing across features of each token to stabilize training dynamics and gradient flow across sub-layers (applied after self-attention and after feed-forward network).

Given corpus: 'I like NLP', 'I like AI', 'I love NLP'. Bigram model with Add-1 Laplace smoothing to find P('I like ML'). Counts: C(I)=3, C(like)=2, C(love)=1, C(NLP)=2, C(AI)=1. C(I, like)=2, C(like, ML)=0. Vocabulary V={I, like, NLP, AI, love} (|V|=5). P(like|I) = (C(I, like)+1)/(C(I)+|V|) = (2+1)/(3+5) = 3/8. P(ML|like) = (C(like, ML)+1)/(C(like)+|V|) = (0+1)/(2+5) = 1/7. P('I like ML') = P(like|I) * P(ML|like) = (3/8) * (1/7) = 3/56.
